items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: I read a passage in Blues People by Leroi Jones, who is now known as Amiri Baraka.

ctx.x: Yeah. It was like Ellington listening to his guys warm up, and using pieces of their warm- up when writing a tune. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-

Yeah. So how did I get to that. So anyway, I read a passage in Blues People by Leroi Jones, who is now known as Amiri Baraka. And in those days, I’m talking about the mid- 70’s, 1975, 1977, there were only two books on the reading list. There were probably a few more. But there was Blues People by Leroi Jones, and then The Music of Black Americans by Eileen Southern. So there weren’t that many. And I remember in the book by Amiri Baraka he talked about Africans brought over here as slaves, and they brought their…

day, I believe, that President Nixon made his visit to China. Before that, there wasn’t an open relationship between China and U.S. because of, you know, China being a communist government, the cold war period.
